verses.gurmukhi: ਆਨ ਹਾਟ ਕੇ ਹਟੂਆ ਲੇਤ ਹੈ ਘਟਾਇ ਮੋਲ ਦੇਤ ਹੈ ਚੜ੍ਹਾਇ ਡਹਕਤ ਜੋਈ ਆਵੈ ਜੀ ॥
verses.translit_en: aan haaT ke haTooaa let hai ghaTai mol dhet hai chaRhai ddahakat joiee aavai jee ||

en.bdb: When a shopkeeper or a trader approaches another but a clever shopkeeper, the later sells his merchandise at a profit and manipulates to buy other's goods at a lesser price.

verses.gurmukhi: ਤਿਨ ਸੈ ਬਨਜ ਕੀਏ ਬਿੜਤਾ ਨ ਪਾਵੈ ਕੋਊ ਟੋਟਾ ਕੋ ਬਨਜ ਪੇਖਿ ਪੇਖਿ ਪਛੁਤਾਵੈ ਜੀ ॥
verses.translit_en: tin sai banaj ke'ee biRataa na paavai kouoo ToTaa ko banaj pekh pekh pachhutaavai jee ||

en.bdb: Dealing with such deceitful shopkeepers cannot be profitable. Every trader repents at conducting a deal at a loss.

verses.gurmukhi: ਕਾਠ ਕੀ ਹਾਂਡੀ ਜੈਸੇ ਚਢੈ ਏਕੈ ਬਾਰਿ ਕੋਊ ਕਪਟ ਬਿਉਹਾਰ ਕੀਏ ਆਪਹਿ ਲਖਾਵੈ ਜੀ ॥
verses.translit_en: kaaTh kee haa(n)ddee jaise chaddai ekai baar kouoo kapaT biauhaar ke'ee aapeh lakhaavai jee ||

en.bdb: Just as a wooden pot can be used for cooking only once, similarly he who indulges in cheating in business exposes his self through his deceitful dealings.

verses.gurmukhi: ਸਤਿਗੁਰ ਸਾਹ ਗੁਨ ਬੇਚ ਅਵਗੁਨ ਲੇਤ ਸੁਨਿ ਸੁਨਿ ਸੁਜਸ ਜਗਤ ਉਠਿ ਧਾਵੈ ਜੀ ॥੪੬੧॥
verses.translit_en: satigur saeh gun bech avagun let sun sun sujas jagat uTh dhaavai jee ||461||

en.bdb: The True Guru is a truthful trader who sells the commodity of virtues and in return takes away vices from Sikhs who come to trade with him. Listening to the glory of the True Guru, the world rushes to Him to obtain this invaluable commodity. (461)
